The Router did not skip any testable checkpoints unjustifiably.
artifact_review: The Router's severity ratings are well-calibrated but perhaps slightly conservative on the 'structural_collapse'. The 'text_gibberish' on the remote (severity 2.5) is supported by the image_text_auditor's failure to extract any text (empty blocks), confirming the text is illegible/melted. The perceptual_quality_auditor noted slight compression, but this is negligible compared to the structural failures. I agree with the Router's identification of these artifacts; they are catastrophic for a product image.
alignment_reasoning: The fine_grained_classifier correctly identifies the class as 'loudspeaker' (Top-1), likely due to the general black-box-and-circle semantic pattern. However, the image fails 7 out of 8 testable diagnostic checkpoints. It lacks the defining physical features of a loudspeaker (proper drivers, enclosure geometry, materials). It is a 'hallucinated' speaker that resembles the class only superficially. Therefore, alignment is very low, barely above random noise, as it fails to represent the functional entity defined in the taxonomy.
artifact_reasoning: The image suffers from severe structural collapse. The main speaker enclosure warps and melts into itself, violating rigid body physics. The base does not ground properly (perspective distortion). Components fuse together (satellite and tower). The remote control features melted buttons and illegible text. These are not minor aesthetic flaws but fundamental generative failures in geometry and topology. The artifact score is very low (close to Reference 1's 1.00) because the object is structurally nonsensical.
